Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Situation2: Assisting at a traffic accident scene to ensure safety and order
Story: My phone buzzed in my pocket as I directed traffic around the twisted metal and flashing lights of the accident scene. The dispatcher’s voice crackled in my earpiece, but I could see the name on my phone: my granddaughter, probably calling to tell me about her first day at her new job. I’d promised her I’d call, promised I’d be there to share her excitement, to be the grandparent who always listened. But right now, horns blared and anxious drivers leaned out their windows, demanding answers. My partner waved me over, needing help with a witness. I felt the weight of my badge and the responsibility to keep everyone safe, but my heart ached at the thought of missing this moment with my family. I stood in the middle of the chaos, torn between the duty to my city and the promise I’d made to my granddaughter, the phone vibrating insistently in my hand.
